A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REMIX research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original factoid-retention experiments with Llama-3-8B and Mistral-7B, including REMIX, replay, ablations, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds regularization comparisons, knowledge-manipulation tests, MMLU evaluation, and quantitative probing results.

M1.justification: REMIX retains the same procedure of mixing random word sequences or generic text into one or both fine-tuning stages. No change to its architecture, training objective, or algorithm is reported.

E1.justification: v2 extends evaluation beyond direct factoid recall to selecting between two keys and modifying a recalled value’s first character (Section 5, Table 5), and adds MMLU downstream evaluation (Table 10). Original training datasets, mixing sources, and familiar-factoid scenarios remain.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated weight regularization using EWC and behavior regularization using a KL penalty. Table 4 compares both against REMIX across KVR, PopQA, and TriviaQA with three factoid stage-2 datasets, substantially broadening the comparisons beyond v1’s replay and mixing alternatives.

E3.justification: The original models, sample counts, exact-match evaluation, mixing ratios, learning rates, batch sizes, and stopping rules remain unchanged. v2 adds testing procedures for two-key selective recall and character replacement, plus a briefly specified MMLU evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of knowledge manipulation and downstream capability preservation, and extends Logit Lens analysis with quantitative layer-of-first-occurrence summaries including PopQA. Figure 4 replaces the previous TriviaQA profile panel with these summaries. Existing mixing-source, length, ratio, familiar-factoid, and three-stage analyses are retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: v2 adds mean and standard-deviation estimates of layer of first occurrence over 100 examples (Figure 4). These describe layer dispersion rather than accuracy uncertainty. Three-run accuracy averaging and the standard-deviation error bars in Appendix B.1 remain unchanged; no increased run count is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds regularization, manipulation, MMLU, and probing results. For example, Table 5 reports factoid selective-recall accuracy of 11.2% for Random/K-Pile versus 0.7% without mixing. Original Table 2, full Mistral results, and replay results remain unchanged. Table 4’s 67.4% KVR REMIX average excludes ID and is not a gain over Table 2’s 53.2%. In the matched mixing-source plot, WebQA values change from 61.4 to 62.7 for Random/- and 70.2 to 70.6 for Random/K-Pile.

T1.justification: The factoid and familiarity definitions, one-step gradient argument, and Appendix A’s replay and REMIX derivations retain the same mathematical content and assumptions. Model-notation changes and naming the existing first-occurrence measure do not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: The continual-memorization setting and central REMIX contribution remain. v2’s abstract and introduction extend the comparative claim beyond replay to other continual-learning baselines and add the claim that robust memorization facilitates knowledge manipulation.

C2.justification: v2 newly discusses the usability of retained knowledge while acknowledging that manipulation remains extremely difficult. It also considers possible disruption of other capabilities from random-word mixing and interprets MMLU results as better preservation relative to no mixing. The original interference explanation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents the EWC minibatch Fisher approximation, KL reference-model penalty, manipulation prompts, and 100-example probing summary. Original training details remain. Both PDFs link to the same repository, including v1’s hyperlink behind the text 'URL'; v2 makes the address explicit and additionally mentions data availability.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds positioning relative to corpus-based continual knowledge learning through Jang et al. (2022) and Seo et al. (2024), while trimming Ghosal’s account and NTK background. Sun et al. (2020) and the MMLU reference support new experiments. The overarching research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, condenses dataset descriptions, changes LLM terminology to LM, and reorganizes the analysis narrative. Several existing main-text ablations move to Appendix B.6, and the appendix subsections are reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, redraws and relocates Figure 1, splits Table 1’s presentation, and changes Figure 4 from two plots to a plot and summary table. It abbreviates the main Mistral table while retaining full results in the appendix, adds three experimental tables, and relocates existing figures.

improvement.justification: The added regularization comparisons, quantitative probing, manipulation tests, and MMLU evaluation strengthen empirical scrutiny while preserving the original evidence. The manipulation study also exposes a useful applicability limitation. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new baseline and MMLU settings, and the manipulation results support only modest practical claims.
